title: Iteration Budget Math
prompt: ISO C. Implement `size_t iters_for_budget(double budget_ms, double per_iter_ms)` — return the number of whole iterations that fit the budget, rounding up (a partially affordable iteration still runs once); return 0 when either argument is <= 0. Implement `double bench_sink(size_t iters)` that accumulates a workload into a local `volatile double sink` (sink += (double)i / 4.0 each iteration) and returns the sink — proving the work was not optimized away.

tests.name: ceil rounding
tests.hint: 10/3 needs 4 iterations to cover the budget; exact division needs exactly 3.

tests.name: degenerate inputs
tests.hint: No budget or no measurable per-iteration cost means run nothing.

tests.name: sink proves work happened
tests.hint: A volatile accumulator survives dead-code elimination: the loop ran.
